public_rationale: Independent reporting confirms the January 2024 IEEE Spectrum publication and its demonstration of recognizable reproductions by Midjourney and DALL-E 3. The outputs were still images. The substantive demonstration holds, but 'video generation software' misstates the medium. Treating that phrase as an incidental wording error would instead support the claim's main point.
limitations: The mixed result turns on retaining the explicit word 'video'.
The selected report describes the authors' demonstration; it is not an independent replication of every example.
Visual resemblance alone does not establish legal infringement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In January, in IEEE Spectrum, Marcus and Reid Southen demonstrated issues similar to the New York Times findings in what he called video generation software, such as Midjourney and Dall-E.

statement.excerpt: In January, in IEEE Spectrum, Reid Southen and I demonstrated similar issues in video generation software, such as Midjourney and Dall-E:
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s Continuing Copyright Problems, an Essay in Memory of Suchir Balaji, 1998 - 2024

from_speaker: Reid Southen and I demonstrated similar issues
our_interpretation: 'Similar issues' means recognizable reproduction of existing visual works or characters.
Assess the publication and demonstration separately from the explicit description of the software as video generation. Do not silently replace 'video' with 'image'.
criteria.support_condition: Independent documentation confirms the January IEEE Spectrum demonstration by both authors, the named systems and recognizable reproductions; full support also requires the stated video medium to be accurate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable documentation contradicts the publication, demonstration, named systems or stated medium. Confirmation of the demonstration alongside an incorrect medium warrants mixed.
